newsitem.title: UK: Steep UK rate rise unlikely after soft PPI report.
newsitem.headline: Steep UK rate rise unlikely after soft PPI report.

text.p: A sharp fall in UK input prices and soft factory gate prices in April suggest headline inflation will edge lower in the future, making it hard for the newly empowered central bank to justify an aggressive rate rise next month, economists said on Monday.
Input prices fell by a seasonally adjusted 1.9 percent in the month and by an unadjusted 10.5 percent in the year to April, a record annual fall.
Output prices rose by 0.2 percent in the month for a year-on-year rise of 0.8 percent compared with 1.0 percent rise in the year to March.

"Producer prices are one of the best indicators of future retail prices that we have and these very soft figures will make it more difficult for the newly independent Bank to jusitify an aggressive monetary tightening," said Alex Garrard, UK economist at UBS.
Michael Saunders, UK economist at Salomon Brothers, said while the link between producer prices and retail prices was not perfect, the weak report suggests a benign outlook for high street prices.
He noted when producer prices surged in 1994, they had little impact on retail prices.

"But the current pattern is much different, with widespread weakness in producer prices across all industry groups, and particularly in areas such as food and fuel that have a quick effect on the RPI."
Saunders agreed that the figures limit the scope for severe rate rises in coming months.

"Low inflation figures, plus extra fiscal restraint, will limit the extent to which rates rise," he said, forecasting only a 25 or 50 basis point tightening in the next few months followed by a period of stability.
Many economists say the Bank will hold back from tightening policy until they see the contents of Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's mini-budget.

"I don't see an early rate rise, firstly because it makes sense to see the budget and secondly because the new monetary policy committee will be meeting for the first time and will want to get a clear view of one another's views," said Garrard.
The government will appoint four outsiders to the new committee before the first meeting.
No date has been set yet for the mini-budget, although there is speculation that it will be on June 10.
Brown has already promised one tax rise, a windall levy on privatised utilities, and one tax cut, on the level of indirect tax on heating fuel.
Economists noted the pound's sharp appreciation has squeezed import prices and allowed core input prices to fall sharply -- by 1.2 percent on the month and 8.2 percent on the year.
The Bank of England has in the past been rather dismissive of the impact sterling upward march will have on inflation.
The pound has gained around 19 percent on a trade-weighted basis since last August.
But earlier on Monday, Bank of England Governor Eddie George said the pound's very strong appreciation was a factor that could help inflation meet the government's 2.5 percent target.
"It looks like the Bank has changed its tune on sterling. The change might suggest a more sanguine inflation report than usual tomorrow," said Garrard.
The Bank will publish its quarterly inflation report at 1030 GMT on Tuesday, the first report since it was granted operational control over interest rates.
